{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting / Interface Agreement)

**Prepared for:** Client (Customer-side review)  
**Playbook review:** 18 rules assessed — 10 compliant, 6 deviations, 2 missing

---

## 1. Executive summary

The commercial architecture of this Agreement is broadly acceptable to us. The rules that most often bite a customer are clean: there is no exclusivity, non-compete, employee non-solicit, MFN or audit right binding Client; there are no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us; Section 14 gives us an unrestricted no-cause termination right with no exit fee; and the auto-renewal mechanic (successive one-year terms, 30 days' non-renewal notice) meets our preferred position. Governing law and venue (California law, San Luis Obispo County courts) sit at the fallback and we do not redline them. The minimum monthly fee in Section 5(a) sits at the fallback because it is confined to the current one-year term and is releasable through our at-will exit.

The risk in this document is concentrated in the risk-allocation and IP provisions, all of which fail even the fallback. Most seriously, the only limitation-of-liability language caps TrueLink alone (and only for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11) while leaving Client's liability entirely uncapped under a very broad Client indemnity — walk-away territory under our playbook. There is no Vendor IP infringement indemnity, no performance or conformance warranty for the Hosting, Support or Interface (only a Year 2000 warranty), no Client-side ownership of the Support Services deliverables we pay for, no insurance undertaking at all despite TrueLink processing consumer credit data, and no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation. The licence grant and assignment clause are also too narrow: no affiliate/contractor scope, no perpetual paid-up licence, and no successor carve-out, so an M&A event would require TrueLink's discretionary approval.

We propose redlines on the six deviations and insertion of the two missing clauses. Two commercial gaps also require completion before signature: the blank monthly minimums in Section 5(a) and the mis-numbered cross-references to "Section 4".

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant runs to Client alone (no affiliates/contractors); no perpetual/irrevocable paid-up licence; § 15 consent has no successor carve-out. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | Licence expressly non-exclusive; § 2(a) preserves our freedom to source elsewhere. § 3(i) credit-report tie-in is narrow and Interface-scoped only. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No stipulated damages, default interest, late fee or early-termination fee. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No restraint on Client; the separate Non-Competition Agreement limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data (runs in our favour). |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 14 gives Client an unrestricted no-cause exit, ~30–60 days, no penalty; TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Section 9 covers Year 2000 only; no professional/workmanlike, conformance, malicious-code or compliance warranty and no remedy. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance / data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No migration assistance, data export, deletion or certification duty; § 13 puts the migration burden on Client. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No vendor audit or usage-verification right; § 6 documentation duty runs in our favour. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law (§ 26) and exclusive California courts (§ 27) are within the fallback; courts, not arbitration. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | The only MFN (§ 6) runs in our favour, with a one-year price freeze. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume caps | Compliant (fallback) | § 5 COMPENSATION. | Minimum monthly fee limited to the one-year term, no shortfall or take-or-pay charge, at-will exit under § 14. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No no-hire or non-solicit covenant on Client; § 7 "solicit" hits are anti-spam only. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | One-year renewals with a 30-day mutual non-renewal right meets the preferred position. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Liability cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | TrueLink capped (Sections 3, 4, 7, 11 only); Client uncapped. No consequential-damages exclusion and no carve-outs. **Walk-away.** |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 12.b is breach-only; no IP infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach or wilful-misconduct indemnity. Client's § 12.a indemnity is open-ended. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance undertaking anywhere, despite TrueLink hosting Client Content and consumer credit data. **Walk-away.** |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | § 2(d) confirms TrueLink ownership only; no Client ownership of paid-for Support Services deliverables and no retention statement for Client IP/data. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 15 requires consent with an affiliate carve-out only: no Client successor/M&A exception, no reasonableness standard, no competitor bar. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These cannot be signed in their current form:

1. **Asymmetric liability (LOL-CAP, § 12 INDEMNITY).** Client's liability is entirely uncapped while TrueLink is capped for four sections only, and Client carries a very broad indemnity. Our position: a mutual, Agreement-wide cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, a mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, and carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement (with Customer payment obligations confirmed not to be damages).
2. **No insurance at all (INSURANCE, § 12 INDEMNITY).** TrueLink hosts the Web Site and processes Client Content and consumer credit data, its § 12(b) indemnity is unbacked, and liability is capped at 12 months' fees. Our position: a new Section 31 requiring CGL (USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate), E&O (USD 2M), cyber/privacy (USD 5M), statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request.
3. **Assignment consent without a successor carve-out (ASSIGN, § 12 INDEMNITY) — approaching walk-away.** As drafted, a merger or sale of substantially all of Client's assets would require TrueLink's discretionary approval. Our position: a Client successor carve-out, a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, a bar on assignment to a competitor, and confirmation that a Client change of control gives TrueLink no termination right.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline package on the six deviations:** LOL-CAP (mutual, Agreement-wide cap with carve-outs), INDEMN (add TrueLink IP infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach and wilful-misconduct indemnity with notice/control/cooperation procedure; narrow § 12.a to Client Content and Client's breach of law), WARRANTY (professional and workmanlike services with a 90-day conformance period, 12 months conformance to documentation for the Interface, software and deliverables, no malicious code, compliance with laws, plus repair/replacement/refund), IP (Client-side ownership subsection with licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP, Client retention of its IP and data, no joint ownership, carving out the § 8(d) Credit Data licence), LICENSE (extend to affiliates and contractors, perpetual and irrevocable paid-up licences, termination only for uncured material breach), and ASSIGN (successor carve-out plus reasonableness standard and competitor bar).
2. **Insert the missing clauses:** the insurance section, and a transition clause after the Termination section covering transition assistance, return of data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion — noting this provision falls within the "Sections 1 and 5 through 30" survival language.
3. **Re-draft the transition insertion before it goes out.** The transition proposal did not clear our internal verification, so it needs manual drafting and a second review pass; the four repaired redlines (LICENSE, WARRANTY, ASSIGN, INDEMN, IP, LOL-CAP, INSURANCE) should also be read once more against the final execution copy.
4. **Close the commercial blanks with the business team:** complete the "not less than $____ per month" minimums in § 5(a), and correct the mis-numbered cross-references to "Section 4" (including § 14's "Subject to Section 4", which could otherwise be read as preserving minimums through the notice period).
5. **Obtain and review the separate Non-Competition Agreement** referenced at § 8(d). It is neither attached nor defined here; we understand it limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data, and we should confirm it imposes no restraint on Client.
6. **Park for a future reopening (not raised now):** New York law and venue in place of San Luis Obispo County, a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder, a cap on renewal price uplift beyond the first-year Hosting freeze, and a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (largely moot while fees are billed monthly in arrears). We would also resist any attempt to broaden the § 3(i) credit-report tie-in beyond Interface-routed transactions."}
